<STRUCT_0001>
In the following, if we write <MATH_0001> we will mean that <MATH_0002>
is a topological group and <MATH_0003> a discrete <MATH_0004>-module with
continuous <MATH_0005>-action and <MATH_0006> is the <MATH_0007>th right derived
functor on the category <MATH_0008> of such <MATH_0009>-modules, see
Definitions <REF_0001> and
<REF_0002>. This includes
the case of an abstract group <MATH_0010>, which simply means that <MATH_0011> is viewed
as a topological group with the discrete topology.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
When the module has a nondiscrete topology, we will use the notation
<MATH_0012> to indicate the continuous cohomology groups
introduced in <REF_0003>, see
Section <REF_0004>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a topological group.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> A <TEXTITOPEN_0001><MATH_0002>-module<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>, sometimes called a <TEXTITOPEN_0002>discrete <MATH_0003>-module<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>,
is an abelian group <MATH_0004> endowed with a left action <MATH_0005>
by group homomorphisms such that <MATH_0006> is continuous when <MATH_0007> is given the
discrete topology.
<STRUCT_0003> A <TEXTITOPEN_0003>morphism of <MATH_0008>-modules<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> <MATH_0009> is a
<MATH_0010>-equivariant homomorphism from <MATH_0011> to <MATH_0012>.
<STRUCT_0004> The category of <MATH_0013>-modules is denoted <MATH_0014>.
<STRUCT_0005>
Let <MATH_0015> be a ring.
<STRUCT_0006>
<STRUCT_0007> An <TEXTITOPEN_0004><MATH_0016>-module<TEXTITCLOSE_0004> is an <MATH_0017>-module <MATH_0018> endowed with
a left action <MATH_0019> by <MATH_0020>-linear maps such that <MATH_0021>
is continuous when <MATH_0022> is given the discrete topology.
<STRUCT_0008> A <TEXTITOPEN_0005>morphism of <MATH_0023>-modules<TEXTITCLOSE_0005> <MATH_0024> is a
<MATH_0025>-equivariant <MATH_0026>-module map from <MATH_0027> to <MATH_0028>.
<STRUCT_0009> The category of <MATH_0029>-modules is denoted <MATH_0030>.
